runner_environment: Windows 10, Python 3.14.2, NumPy 2.4.2 (CPU-only, no GPU). Data sourced from the local private mirror at C:/Users/MSI-Vector/Documents/repositories/master-thesis-repository/data because the repository ignores data/* by design.

implementation.method: NumPy MLP scorer trained with RankNet pairwise logistic loss on positive > negative resume preferences within each vacancy; features are hashed token counts over the vacancy text, the resume text and their intersection plus five length / overlap scalars (1541-dim).

pair_construction.comment: Most train vacancies have only one labeled candidate, so the pairwise objective is extremely data-sparse. This is a property of the dataset, not the RankNet implementation.

test_metrics_from_12_baseline_comparison.source: experiments/results/four_model_baseline_test.json (precision@K normalises by K, identical normalisation as BM25 / bi-encoder rows)

comparison_against_other_models_on_test_.cross_encoder: Not re-run in this checkout (no cross_encoder_rubert_tiny2 artifact); historical value from three_model_baseline_test.json is 0.9356 AP.

interpretation: On per-query ranking metrics (precision@1, ndcg@3, mrr@3) RankNet matches BM25 essentially exactly because the hashed token overlap features carry the same lexical signal that BM25 uses; on global pair-AP RankNet is even slightly below BM25 (0.324 vs 0.394) and far below the fine-tuned bi-encoder (0.992).

The bottleneck is the dataset, not the model: only 4 out of 2343 training vacancies contain both a positive and a negative labeled resume, yielding 48 preference pairs in total. This is far too few examples for a pairwise Learning-to-Rank objective to surpass a tuned semantic bi-encoder trained with ContrastiveLoss on 4176 binary pairs.

Methodological value: the offline experiment closes the loop between the Learning-to-Rank discussion in the thesis and the experimental protocol; it demonstrates that pairwise L2R is the correct method but that production deployment requires either (a) richer per-vacancy candidate lists with graded relevance, or (b) hybrid features (BM25 score, bi-encoder cosine, structured signals) instead of pure hashed text.
